decisive_tests: build_failed: functional suite did not compile (public parse_image_url/parse_audio_url/parse_video_url signatures changed; E0061)

b1.summary: Five runs pass 13/13 security tests and fail the same 3 functional tests. Each made the public library loaders (util::parse_image_url/parse_audio_url, video::parse_video_url) refuse local paths and file: URLs, moved local loading to new *_local/*_allow_local functions, repointed the CLI, and in several runs edited the project's own test_parse_image_url. MiMo run 2 added a mandatory SourceAccess argument to the same public loaders, so the hidden suite failed to compile (build_failed; security not measured). No run left a measured security hole.

distinct_decisive_tests: build_failed (signature coupling of the same public loaders)

b4.note: The same design decision in all 6 runs: change the semantics (5) or the signature (1) of the public media loaders instead of adding a request-side policy. The same 3 tests fail every time. No run is one test short, but every run is one design choice short.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md: 'confirm that the harness may depend on the unchanged public signatures of parse_image_url/parse_audio_url/parse_video_url and on ChatCompletionParseContext's field set under K'. The fun_local_* tests are rated medium risk. MiMo run 2 is exactly that signature-coupling case (build_failed, audit medium). No sign-off is recorded; repairs are all 0.

b6.reason: The decisive trap is T5 (keep the public loaders local-permissive). The published fix 74793379 does this explicitly: parse_image_url/parse_audio_url/parse_video_url keep MediaSourcePolicy::Local, and new server-policy variants are used by parse_request (checks/upstream_fix.patch lines 583-632, 741-786). notes.md: 'The reader's design (T1, T3, T4, T5) is entirely covered by the published fix'. The upstream patch scores 0.8462 with functional green. Only the injected T8 (on-disk attachment path) is outside upstream, and every model already closed it. A model that looks up the fix very likely solves this.

c1.mechanism: SSRF + local file read via request-supplied media/attachment sources

c2.pattern: over-blocked legitimate use (changed shared public API)
c2.note: Manifest origin of T5 is published_fix_far_site. Models secured all 13 request routes, including the audio/video copies, the IPv6/mapped/name-resolved attachment URL and the injected file_path. They did it by making the shared public loaders strict, which breaks in-process library callers. The instruction never mentions in-process or library callers, only K.

e2.why: All 6 audits trustworthy and model-failed; 5 high, 1 medium (mimo run 2, build_failed).

e3.why: READY, but the human-review question on public-signature coupling is open, and one run (mm2) was decided by exactly that coupling.

e4.why: No decisive security miss: 13/13 security in 5 runs; run 6 did not compile. All failures are keep-working.

e5.why: The upstream fix keeps the public loaders on a Local policy and adds server variants, which is exactly the decisive behaviour.

concerns: Pure keep-working breaker: 0 security misses. The only uncovered-upstream element (injected T8) was solved by every model.
Upstream covers the decisive trap: an open-internet model that reads 74793379 copies the Local/ServerRequest policy split and passes functional, so it probably does not survive open internet.
Fragile: the same 3 functional tests (one design choice: the public loader semantics) decide all 5 graded runs; T5 is the whole breaker.

Decisive tests call product library functions directly (util::parse_image_url, video::parse_video_url) as 'trusted in-process callers'. The instruction says nothing about library/in-process callers. Fairness relies on K covering public API behaviour, and the models did keep the in-repo CLI working by repointing it.
MiMo run 2 is a compile failure from a signature change (harness coupling). FAIRNESS.md left this as an open human question.
No blind fix (blind_status error 3), so solvability rests on the oracle and the builder's own pass-alt and pass-hardening.
one_line: mistral.rs media SSRF: both models closed every request route (13/13 security) but made the shared public media loaders refuse local files, breaking in-process callers. The upstream fix shows exactly how to avoid this.
